# Retail POS 3.0.0-RC1

Retail POS 3.0.0-RC1 is the first release candidate of the modernized retail-focused POS. It turns the long-standing Openbravo POS foundation into a more maintainable, operator-friendly product for shops that need dependable checkout, practical catalogue operations, and clearer day-to-day controls.

## What this release enables

### Faster, clearer checkout operations

- Staff can keep open tickets live across tills, reducing confusion when a sale is started at one workstation and completed at another.
- Payment options, split payments, refunds, account payments, vouchers, discounts, and loyalty rewards are presented more clearly and follow the amount the customer actually pays.
- Sellers are selected consistently, can be recognized quickly, and retain a stable button order, reducing avoidable mistakes during busy trading periods.
- Confirmation dialogs, action labels, product buttons, and login screens use clearer language and layouts that are easier to operate on touch screens.
- Unknown barcode scans now guide the operator instead of interrupting the sale with an unhelpful data-entry flow.

### Better catalogue and stock productivity

- Missing products can be created directly from the catalogue data at the till, including complete product families with size and colour variants.
- Purchase costs, markup rules, tax-inclusive selling prices, brand overrides, and rounding rules support more consistent pricing decisions.
- Replenishment workflows, opening stock capture, model-level stock and sales views, and category-based reporting make it easier to keep the shop supplied and understand what is selling.
- Catalogue tools can load shared fallback data, import supplier pricing, preserve invoice references, and update products in bulk without requiring manual database work.
- Catalogue and report behaviour is more predictable for duplicate category names, multiple supplier/catalogue variants, and products without images.

### Safer administration and customer service

- Integrated customer management supports customer search, editing, account payments, loyalty configuration, and more reliable customer-to-ticket handling.
- Role-based sales and administration modes, seller permissions, employee account-payment permissions, and privileged operations provide better control over who can perform sensitive actions.
- Daily database backups can be configured and scheduled from the application, while existing databases can be adopted and upgraded through Flyway without replacing shop data.
- Receipt, printer, drawer, customer-display, and store-resource configuration is kept separate from the application build, making updates safer for existing installations.

### More dependable operations and support

- Rotating application logs, richer update diagnostics, copyable error details, and improved Flyway diagnostics make incidents easier to investigate.
- The local updater preserves configuration and databases while replacing only the application files, and verifies downloaded packages with SHA256 checksums.
- The build is now based on Gradle with reproducible dependency resolution, Java 8-compatible application bytecode, modern JDK 21 build tooling, and automated formatting checks.
- Database migrations and representative data are verified against Derby, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, including empty installations, legacy database adoption, and repeated migration runs.
- Legacy packaging and unused ERP, web, restaurant, and generated surfaces have been removed so the product and maintenance scope are focused on retail POS use cases.

## Distribution

This release candidate is distributed as portable x86_64 packages for Linux, Windows, and Intel macOS. Windows and macOS packages include a bundled Java runtime; the Linux package uses the system Java installation. Every package includes a SHA256 checksum.

Native installers, Apple Silicon support, Linux ARM64 support, and platform signing remain planned follow-up work.
